nodes.meaning: Given any compact smooth PI test g, set f=g-integral g d pi. Prove f is bounded smooth, centered, with compact gradient support. Do not claim compact support for f.
For bounded centered f, construct the actual law with density 1+epsilon*f; obtain eventual a.e. lower bound 1/2 and mass one, including M=0.
Genuine calculus for q(u)=u log u-u+1 yields q(1+t)/t^2 -> 1/2.
For finite mu and a.e.-strongly-measurable a.e.-bounded f, produce the f^2 envelope and integral limit. No centering, smoothness, probability normalization or gradient assumption is needed here.

Identify the actual density/Radon-Nikodym derivative, prove finite canonical KL and use zero mean to remove the linear compensator. This bounded centered form covers both the literal hint and the broader second consumer.
Extend the assumed compact-test LSI to the actual u=sqrt(1+epsilon*f), using proved cutoffs/limits/admissibility. The test is noncompact even when f is compact. Positivity alone is insufficient.
Derive square-gradient integrability from the bounded smooth compact-gradient class and finite probability measure. Bounded f alone is not enough.
Compute the genuine gradient of the positive density and derive the dominated limit of integral ||grad f||^2/(1+epsilon*f).
Apply the extended LSI to the constructed density, keeping the coefficient C/2 and actual finite energy; do not assume the desired comparison.
Divide the valid LSI by epsilon^2 and take both limits: integral f^2 <= C integral ||grad f||^2 on the bounded centered compact-gradient class.
Use the proved centered-test PI with f=g-integral g. Identify integral f^2 with Var(g) and grad f with grad g. Discharge, rather than assume, the centered-PI premise.
The exact compact Euclidean PI target above, with the same admissible C, not equality of optimal constants.
L2/form-domain core/closure extension and abstract reversible-energy route remain unproved. The compact Euclidean subtarget does not certify all of Exercise 1.7.
